commits.message: Add LICENSE file
chore: update readme
fix: cargo keywords

feat(ui): detect account type from credentials.json subscriptionType

Replaces the hardcoded ENDPOINT_DEFAULT constant with a runtime lookup
of `claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType` from each profile's credentials.json,
title-casing the value (e.g. "pro" → "Pro", "claude_max" → "Claude Max").
Falls back to "Pro" when credentials are absent or the field is missing.

feat(usage): fetch and display 5-hour usage bar at startup

Adds a new `usage` module that calls `GET /api/oauth/usage` with the
OAuth access token from each profile's credentials. Profiles are fetched
in parallel at startup (4s connect / 8s recv timeouts) and results stored
transiently on `Profile.usage`.

The 5-hour utilization is rendered as a 10-block ANSI bar in both the
main menu list and the profile submenu title:
  [████████░░] 62%   (dim when <60%, yellow ≥60%, red ≥80%)

Profiles without OAuth credentials or with a custom base URL are
silently skipped. Fetch failures are ignored — usage simply shows nothing.

feat(usage): persist usage to disk and fall back to cache on rate limit

On a successful fetch the result is written to
~/.clauth/profiles/<name>/usage_cache.json. On any fetch failure
(429, timeout, network error) the cache is read instead, so the
bar keeps showing after the first successful run even when the
OAuth usage endpoint is temporarily unavailable.
docs: update README for usage bar and subscription type detection

feat: symlink ~/.claude/.credentials.json to active profile

Replace write_claude_credentials (file copy) with a symlink so Claude
Code's token refreshes go directly to the profile's credentials.json.
Falls back to file copy on Windows without symlink privilege.

Also fixes dangling-symlink cases on rename and delete of active profile.

fix(actions): validate profile name to block path traversal

- Restrict profile names to ASCII alphanumerics, '-', '_', '.'
- Reject leading '.' so dotfile-like names cannot escape the profiles dir
- Prevents names like 'foo/bar' or '..' from being created under ~/.clauth/profiles/

fix(actions): persist state before destructive filesystem ops

- rename_profile: save profiles.toml before re-linking credentials so a
  failed link leaves disk state pointing at the renamed directory instead
  of an unloadable old name
- delete_profile: save profiles.toml after removing the entry from state
  but before removing the directory and credentials symlink, so a failed
  fs cleanup cannot leave state referencing a missing profile

fix(usage): ensure cache parent dir exists before writing

Before writing usage_cache.json, create the parent profile directory if
missing. Previously the write failed silently for profiles whose dir had
not yet been created on disk, so a fresh fetch was discarded.

feat(usage): refresh utilization in the background every 30s

- Introduce UsageStore (Arc<Mutex<HashMap>>) and TokenList shared between
  the main loop and a background ticker thread.
- Replace the one-shot startup fetch with usage::fetch_all_into for the
  initial parallel sync, then spawn_refresher loops every 30s.
- The token list is re-derived after each main-menu action so renames,
  additions, and deletions are picked up by the next tick.
- Each menu rebuild pulls the latest snapshot from the store; visible
  refresh happens between user interactions, since inquire's Select
  blocks the screen while a prompt is open.

feat(menu): rerender main menu during usage refresh

Replace the main inquire Select prompt with a small crossterm loop so the
menu can redraw while usage data changes in the background. The submenu
still uses inquire, and the main menu keeps the same labels, highlight
style, and navigation keys while adding periodic refresh ticks.

fix(menu): wrap cursor at menu boundaries

Make Up/k from the first main-menu item jump to the last item, and Down/j
from the last item jump back to the first. This matches common terminal
menu behavior and keeps Home/End unchanged.

refactor(menu): simplify cursor handling in main menu rendering

- Removed unnecessary cursor position handling and restored functionality.
- Updated `render_main_menu` to accept row parameter for better control.
- Improved code clarity and maintainability by consolidating cursor operations.

fix(menu): adjust cursor handling in raw mode initialization

Ensure the cursor position is consistent after enabling raw mode by
calculating the necessary lines needed for scrolling. This prevents
visual discrepancies during menu rendering.

feat(completions): implement shell completion scripts for bash, zsh, and fish

Add support for command-line completions in clauth for bash, zsh, and fish shells. This includes functions to print completion scripts and install them into the user's shell configuration.

fix(menu): clear terminal artifacts after menu interactions

Ensure the terminal is cleared of any artifacts left by the menu
prompt before re-rendering, improving user experience during
profile submenu navigation.

feat(usage): show reset times and detect actual plan tier

`subscriptionType` in OAuth credentials misreports Max accounts as Pro.
Pull plan info from `/api/oauth/profile` so the menu shows the real
tier — Max 5x / Max 20x / Pro / Team / Enterprise / Free — and surface
when each rate-limit window resets.
docs: describe new plan detection and reset-time display
feat(menu): quit on Q in the main menu

feat(oauth): refresh access tokens on startup

Hits the same `/v1/oauth/token` flow Claude Code uses at launch so the
5-hour usage window starts ticking without an inference call. Refresh
tokens rotate on every call, so the new pair is persisted back to each
profile's credentials.json before the usage fetch runs.

feat(oauth): refresh only profiles missing a 5h timer and re-fetch

Previously refreshed every profile on every launch, churning refresh
tokens that didn't need rotation. Now the initial usage fetch decides
which profiles lack a running window; only those get a token refresh,
then their usage is re-queried so the timer shows up in the menu —
confirming the refresh actually started it.

feat(oauth): kick the 5h timer with an opt-in Haiku ping

Token refresh alone doesn't start the 5-hour window — confirmed
experimentally against /api/oauth/usage, /v1/oauth/token,
/v1/messages/count_tokens, and a handful of session endpoints. Only
a real /v1/messages call starts it.

Add `kick_timer = true` per-profile in config.toml; on startup, for
each opted-in profile with no running window, refresh the OAuth pair
and send a max_tokens=1 Haiku message (~22 in, 1 out tokens). Then
re-fetch usage so the menu confirms the timer is now visible.
fix(ui): adjust extra usage chunk formatting for better precision
chore(gitignore): add scripts directory to .gitignore

feat(profile): backfill config.toml with documented templates

Auto-create or repopulate empty config.toml files on profile load with
commented examples for every available option (base_url, api_key,
kick_timer), so users discover settings without consulting the README.
Subsequent saves preserve the comment hints alongside written values.

Also hide plan and usage chunks from API-endpoint profile rows in both
the main list and the per-profile submenu — those numbers come from
OAuth /usage and don't apply when traffic goes through a custom proxy.

feat(menu): add weekly usage display in profile entries

Introduce weekly usage metrics in the profile menu, enhancing user visibility of usage data. This includes calculations for weekly bar widths and conditional rendering based on available data.

refactor: tighten serde, error, and locking conventions

No behavior change. Struct-level `rename_all`, typed GitHub release
parsing, named Mutex panics, shared anyhow helper, `u64` for durations.

feat(profile): apply per-profile env vars to settings.json

The dedicated base_url / api_key fields only patched ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. Profiles can now declare an `[env]` table in
config.toml whose keys are merged on switch and cleared when switching
away. Profile-declared keys win over base_url / api_key so users can
override either through env when needed.

feat(oauth): rate-limit kick_timer to one kick per ~4.5h

Previously every launch with kick_timer = true would refresh the OAuth
pair and fire a Haiku ping whenever the usage endpoint showed no active
5-hour window. A stale or briefly-unreachable usage endpoint after a
successful kick caused us to re-spend the kick on every launch. Persist
the last kick time per profile and skip rekicks until the 5h window
would have rolled over.
chore: release v0.1.7

feat(fallback): implement automatic account switching based on utilization

Add a fallback chain feature that allows profiles to automatically switch
when their 5-hour utilization exceeds a specified threshold. This includes
menu options for managing the fallback chain and setting thresholds per profile.

chore: release v0.1.8

fix: serialize concurrent state writes across clauth instances

Multiple clauth instances racing on the same files could clobber each
other's writes to profiles.toml and ~/.claude/settings.json, double-spend
OAuth refresh tokens during startup kicks, and fight over the
.credentials.json symlink. Add an advisory file lock at ~/.clauth/.lock
held briefly around every state mutation, route writes through a
tempfile+rename helper so concurrent readers never see partial files,
and claim each kick's cooldown slot before the network call so a racing
instance observes the rotation and skips. The menu now reloads
profiles.toml when its mtime changes so edits from another instance
become visible without a restart.

feat(menu): underline profile name when usage is stale or unavailable

Surface the usage-fetch outcome at the profile-name level: yellow
underline when the API refused this tick and the bars come from the
on-disk cache, red underline when the API failed and no cache exists.
The underline color uses SGR 58 (colored underline); terminals that
don't understand it still render a plain underline as a fallback
signal. OAuth profiles only — API-key profiles don't poll usage.

fix(tui): drop just_auto_started debounce that could stall auto-start

The flag was meant to swallow the busy→idle edge produced by the
follow-up manual_refresh, but when that fetch completed inside one
100ms poll window the edge was never observed and the flag stayed
true. The next real refresh tick then consumed its own edge and
auto-start lost a cycle. Per-profile last_auto_start_at cooldown
already prevents re-kicking the same window, so a second
auto_start_windows call from the manual_refresh edge is a no-op.

fix(cli): kick named profile's 5h window on clauth <name> switch

Add oauth::auto_start_named: cooldown-gated refresh + kick for one
profile. The bare switch arm now invokes it after switch_profile so
an opt-in profile (auto_start = true) gets its 5h timer primed
without requiring the TUI. The 4.5h cooldown stops repeat CLI
switches from re-firing inside an active window.

fix(auth): adopt a blank profile's first login so `which` resolves it

A credential-less profile gains no symlink target on activation, so Claude Code's fresh login lands in a standalone file the profile never owned. Adopt that first login on snapshot/divergence-poll, and as a read-time fallback attribute an unmatched live login to the credential-less active profile.

fix(which): resolve started profile inside clauth start sessions

A credential-less profile started via `clauth start` has no refresh-token match until the watchdog adopts its first login, and the in-session guard suppressed the credential-less fallback — so `clauth which` printed unknown. Resolve the started profile directly from the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR runtime path (.../profiles/<name>/runtime), which works even with no stored credentials.

fix(usage): correct AIMD cadence, cover state machine end-to-end

Cache-hit detection now requires the poll to land inside the server-side
cache window — at NORMAL or slower, unchanged values mean idle, not cache,
so the learner can drift below NORMAL instead of snapping back on every
pause. Rotated tokens are propagated into the live TokenList so a 401
retry can't burn the refresh chain while waiting for the mtime reload.

refactor(usage): split into fetch and scheduler modules

scheduler.rs owns the AIMD learner because only the scheduler ever
observes fetch outcomes and feeds them into update_learner; making it
its own module would push FetchOutcome, apply_outcome, the cache-hit
math, and all the AIMD state aliases out as pub(crate) for no benefit.
feat(tui): per-profile activity store and spinner with refresh visibility

feat(tui): rotate-all and on-tick refresh off the UI thread

oauth fns now take &Arc<Mutex<AppConfig>> + OpResultSender; per-profile
workers acquire/release the lock around HTTP and stream OpResult on
completion. RotateAll, on-tick auto_start_named, and on-tick rotate_one
each dispatch a worker thread; the UI thread drains results, toasts
per-name outcomes, and rebuilds usage_tokens when any refresh landed.
Input gates: is_idle blocks per-profile Switch, any_busy blocks RotateAll.

feat(tui): background startup with non-blocking first paint

Move reconcile-probe HTTP and the bootstrap (relink, refresh-all, initial
fetch, auto-start kicks) onto worker threads sequenced through a new
StartupSignal channel drained in on_tick, so the event loop paints before
any network or FS walk runs.

perf(runtime): shrink watchdog mirror_tree lock scope in fake mode

mirror_tree now runs lockless; only mirror_credentials stays under the
state lock. copy_file writes via atomic_write so a concurrent reader never
sees torn bytes.

feat(runtime): per-profile `.claude.json` with cross-profile sync

Each profile runtime gets its own `.claude.json` instead of a shared
symlink, so Claude Code's cached `oauthAccount` (plus billing caches)
no longer leaks one account's identity into another. A background
syncer converges all other (shared) fields last-write-wins; old shared
symlinks are migrated to copies on acquire.

fix(usage): stop AIMD learner oscillating on idle profiles

An idle Fresh poll above the server-cache TTL was neither a cache hit nor
a genuine util change, yet the recovery arm bumped the interval down every
time, dropping it below TTL where the cache-hit arm snapped it back up.
Thread a util_changed signal so bump_down fires only on real movement; an
unchanged-util Fresh is now a learner no-op.

extends RotationGuard to refresh_all workers, run_auto_start, and
fetch_with_rotation's 401 leg so a concurrent clauth start cannot
double-spend a single-use refresh token. force=true still guards but
rotates live profiles; scheduler 401 leg gains a has_live_session check.

fix(oauth): make token rotation crash-durable via staged credentials

Stage the rotated pair to credentials.json.pending before save_profile and
adopt it on next load when the commit never lands; write credentials.json
before config.toml. A failed save or crash no longer strands the chain.

feat(lockorder): enforce global lock acquisition order with RankedMutex

Every shared lock is a RankedMutex<T, RANK>; the state flock and RotationGuard
carry ranks too. Acquiring out of rank debug-panics and is compiled out in
release, replacing the prose lock-order discipline.

opted-in background profile, which previously only got a one-shot

windowless_auto_start_candidates treated any present resets_at as a live
window; an expired-but-uncleared timestamp kept a background profile from
ever being re-kicked, so only the active profile (refreshed by Claude Code)
auto-started. Require resets_at to be in the future, matching
scan_expired_windows.

refactor(oauth): drop proactive token rotation at window-expiry, bootstrap, switch

These paths spent a single-use refresh token eagerly; the fetch path's
401-recovery already rotates lazily when an access token actually expires, so
the eager spends were redundant and added double-spend surface. Remove the 5h
window-expiry rotation subsystem (scan + queue + rotate_one_for_window +
LastRotatedWindow), the bootstrap refresh_all leg, and the switch worker's
rotate_one calls. The switch is now a synchronous UI-thread relink (no worker,
no OpResult round-trip).

refactor(cli): stop rotating tokens on CLI switch, drop dead rotate_one

The TUI switch already dropped eager rotation; the CLI switch
(switch_profile_cli) was the last caller still rotating the outgoing/incoming
chains. Remove it so both UIs share one token-rotation policy: lazy 401-recovery
on the fetch path (or Claude Code on launch). The shared switch mutation
(switch_profile / switch_profile_reconciled) was already common to both. With
its last production caller gone, drop the rotate_one wrapper and repoint its
test to rotate_one_inner.

docs: drop proactive-rotation narrative; switch is a sync relink

README + scheduler enum doc no longer claim tokens refresh on launch/switch or
rotate at window expiry; rotation is lazy (401-recovery + the t force-rotate-all)
and switching is an instant on-thread relink.

fix(macos): force-relink on switch so a captured mirror isn't refused

The divergence fix (af6a120) routed the normal macOS switch from the reconcile
(force) path to the plain `switch_profile` path — which then bailed in
`link_profile_credentials` with "refusing to replace .credentials.json — live
file differs from profile 'X'; resolve divergence first" on EVERY `clauth <name>`.

Root cause: on macOS `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is always a regular-file
Keychain mirror of the ACTIVE account, so it legitimately differs from the switch
target. The non-force guard compares live-vs-target bytes and can't tell a
captured mirror from an uncaptured re-login.

`switch_profile` now snapshots the outgoing creds (which captures every state
except an uncaptured re-login) and then FORCE-relinks — safe because the live
file has just been captured into the active profile. The non-force refuse-guard
is kept only for a genuine uncaptured re-login (Diverged & not first-login),
which is reachable only via the scheduler (no pre-check), where refusing rather
than dropping the fresh /login chain is the safe outcome. Interactive callers
already route a real divergence to the reconcile path, so behavior there is
unchanged.

Regression test: a plain .credentials.json matching the active profile (the macOS
mirror) + switch to another profile must succeed and link to the target.
445 pass, clippy -D warnings clean.

feat(macos): route account switches through the Keychain

On macOS, Claude Code reads its OAuth login from the login Keychain
(a generic password: service "Claude Code-credentials"), NOT from
~/.claude/.credentials.json — so clauth's symlink swap is cosmetic there:
Claude Code keeps reading the Keychain and the switch never takes effect
on a running session.

This adds a write-only Keychain integration that makes a switch real:

- src/keychain.rs — write/delete Claude Code's login item via Apple's
  /usr/bin/security CLI. Deliberately the CLI, not the security-framework
  crate: macOS binds a Keychain "Always Allow" grant to the calling
  binary's code signature, and a cargo-built binary's ad-hoc signature
  changes every rebuild (so a grant never persists). Routing through
  Apple's stable, code-signed /usr/bin/security makes the one-time grant
  stick across clauth rebuilds. A 20s wall-clock deadline kills a stuck
  invocation (unanswered ACL prompt / locked keychain) so it can't wedge
  the caller.
- claude.rs wires the write on link/force-link and a delete on clear,
  behind #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] + keychain::enabled().

Write-only by design: clauth stores each profile's credentials as a file
and never reads Claude Code's Keychain item in any automatic path (reading
it prompts on every call). enabled() is false under cfg(test), so the
suite keeps the file/symlink model and never touches the real login item;
the KC-1 round-trip test drives a throwaway service and is #[ignore]d.

macOS-only: the module and every call site are cfg-gated, so non-macOS
builds are unchanged.

feat(oauth): self-contained browser OAuth login

Upstream's `clauth login` runs Claude Code's own `/login` inside the
profile's runtime and adopts the credentials file the runtime watchdog
reads. On macOS that fails: a fresh `/login` under a custom
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR writes only a per-config-dir hashed Keychain item
(`Claude Code-credentials-<hash>`), never `.credentials.json`, so clauth
reports "no login detected — profile still has no credentials" (verified
on-device; see #1, #3).

Replace it with a self-contained login that reproduces Claude Code's own
PKCE + RFC 8252 loopback flow: authorize at claude.com, bind a loopback
listener on 127.0.0.1:<random port>, open the browser, catch the redirect,
exchange the code at platform.claude.com, and write the minted tokens
straight into a fresh profile. No dependency on Claude Code's
platform-specific credential storage — works identically on Linux, macOS,
and Windows.

- src/oauth.rs: exchange_code + login token endpoint; CLIENT_ID now

feat(keychain): feed the write to security -i over stdin — token out of argv

Answers the non-blocking note on #18: `security -i` was suspected to
mangle JSON's embedded quotes. Pinned its tokenizer rules empirically on
macOS 15 (throwaway service names only):

- an UNQUOTED value splits on whitespace (usage error) — the suspicion
  holds for any payload with spaces
- wrapped in `"…"` with `\` → `\\` and `"` → `\"`, arbitrary JSON
  (spaces, embedded quotes, backslashes) round-trips byte-identical
- `-U` add-or-update behaves identically through `-i`
- the inner command's exit code propagates as security's own
  (0 success / 44 errSecItemNotFound / 2 usage)

So `write_at` now builds the add-generic-password line, quotes each
field via the new `security_quote` (loud refusal on embedded newlines —
`-i` is a line protocol, a `\n` in a value would parse as a second
command), and pipes it to `security -i`: the token never appears in
argv, closing the process-exec-log (Endpoint Security es_event_exec_t /
EDR) residual the argv-tradeoff doc accepted. Grant binding is
unchanged — the caller is still /usr/bin/security. `read_at`
(test-only) and `delete_at` stay argv (secret-free).

Tests: `run_with_deadline` grows an `stdin_payload` arg (a /bin/cat
EOF test proves the write + pipe-close), `security_quote` unit tests,
and the KC-1 --ignored round-trip re-run against the real Keychain on
a throwaway service including a hostile spaces+quotes+backslash secret.

fix(fallback): weekly (7d) cap hard-blocks a chain member — both directions

Auto-fallback switched INTO an account whose 7d window was spent to
100%. Every exhaustion predicate read only the 5h window — and a
weekly-dead account is the pathological case for that: requests are
refused, so its 5h window drains and then LAPSES (resets_at: null),
which the 5h-only logic reads as fresh headroom. Observed live
2026-07-08: two chain members at exactly 7d=100.0 with no live 5h
window; the walk targeted one, and find_recovered_member relinked
weekly-dead members on every 5h rollover.

Fix: a live seven_day window at >= 100% (WEEKLY_BLOCK_PCT) counts the
account exhausted in every predicate — profile-side and store-side,
target walk and ACTIVE side (hard block trumps burn-aware projection:
nothing left to project), and recovery never picks a weekly-dead
member. soonest_resume reports the WEEKLY reset for such members
instead of bailing on their absent 5h window. Deliberately a hard-block
check, not a threshold: 99.9% still serves requests, and a lapsed
weekly reset is a renewed quota. Per-model weekly_scoped limits (e.g.
"7d fable" at 100 while 7d has room) block only that model, and the
walk can't know which model the next session drives — only the overall
seven_day window gates.

fix(auth): rotation coherence — clauth owns the active Keychain chain

On macOS the running claude re-reads the Keychain per request, so the
live login and clauth's profile copy are two independent refresh chains
of ONE single-use-refresh OAuth family: whichever side refreshes first
revokes the other. Observed on-device 2026-07-07 in both directions —
clauth's rotation won and the running claude hit "Not logged in" at its
stale token's expiry while every clauth copy stayed green; earlier
rounds CC won and clauth's stored refresh tokens came back revoked.

Fix makes clauth deliberately win and keep the live login fresh:

- apply_rotated_tokens_locked (the choke point every rotation site
  shares) mirrors the ACTIVE profile's fresh pair into the Keychain,
  inside the same locked section as the persist so a concurrent switch
  cannot re-point the item in between. Gate: live_login_is_foreign — a
  live .credentials.json that is merely CC's stale regular-file mirror
  of OUR OWN pre-rotation pair still mirrors (the case that matters); a
  genuinely foreign CC re-login is never overwritten.
- fetch_with_rotation rotates the active Keychain-installed profile
  PROACTIVELY (ACTIVE_ROTATE_LEAD_MS = 30 min ahead of expiry) instead
  of waiting for a 401 — reactive rotation loses the race to a live
  session, and a bigger lead costs an earlier rotation, not an extra
  one. Early rotation bails fall back to the plain fetch so proactivity
  never costs a live usage poll. No-op on Linux/Windows (the symlinked
  profile file IS the live credential — no second chain to race) and
  for inactive profiles.

596 tests, clippy clean, rustfmt clean.

feat(auth): unmask dead logins behind 429s, quarantine auth_broken accounts

A dead account (refresh token revoked / login silently dropped) often
surfaces as HTTP 429, not 401 — and a poller that treats every 429 as
"endpoint busy, serve cache" hides a dead login forever behind stale
cached usage. Three pieces close that hole:

- 429 unmasking: a 429 on a token that is ALSO past its clock expiry
  falls through to the rotation leg instead of backing off — a valid
  token behind a real endpoint rate limit still never spends the
  single-use refresh. refresh_result preserves the permanent-vs-
  transient distinction (400/401/403 from the token endpoint = revoked;
  transport/429/5xx = transient); the existing refresh() keeps its
  anyhow signature for current callers.
- Quarantine: a terminally-failed refresh flags the profile in a
  persisted AppState::auth_broken list (transition-logged, once). A
  quarantined member is excluded from every fallback-chain walk
  (next_target + next_auto_switch_target via the ChainSnapshot) and
  refused as a CLI switch target through the ensure_installable
  pre-install gate — a dead token installed into the macOS Keychain
  signs out every running claude. The gate also refreshes a merely
  expiring target before install so a fresh switch never lands on a
  401. Transient failures refuse the one attempt without quarantining.
- Recovery: a successful refresh or a `clauth login <name>`
  (new-capture or in-place reauth) clears the flag.

Also hardens the token-endpoint parse errors while touching them: a 2xx
body that fails to deserialize contains live tokens, so parse failures
now report only category/position/status/length (token_parse_error)
instead of echoing the body — covers the new refresh_result and the
pre-existing exchange_code site.

feat(auth): adopt the live session's rotation — never bet on winning the race

Review round: a fixed proactive lead is a race heuristic — any margin
silently loses to a future Claude Code that refreshes earlier. v2 makes
correctness independent of timing:

- Adopt, don't fight: CC maintains ~/.claude/.credentials.json as a
  regular-file mirror of its Keychain login — a prompt-free read path to
  CC's current pair. When the ACTIVE profile's mirror holds a FRESHER
  pair, try_adopt_live_rotation adopts it into the profile store instead
  of spending our single-use refresh token against a superseded family.
  Identity-guarded: the mirror token's account uuid (/api/oauth/profile)
  must match the profile's cached anchor (seeded at login, backfilled on
  every adopt) or the stored token's own uuid while it still works — a
  manual CC /login into a DIFFERENT account is never captured
  unattended; that stays the TUI divergence flow's job.
- Adopt runs at rotation-leg entry (before spending) and on a refresh
  failure (before falling back) — the same path re-runs every poll, so a
  lagging store self-heals as soon as the mirror catches up (at latest
  CC's next launch).
- The proactive lead is reframed from a magic 30-minute margin to an
  interval-derived invariant — "the Keychain never holds an expired
  token while the poller is alive" (3 poll intervals, 3-min floor). CC
  refreshes only when the token it reads looks spent, so keeping the
  item fresh removes its reason to refresh entirely; if it refreshes
  anyway, the adopt path absorbs it.

fix(fallback): AUTH-4 — a dead login is itself a switch trigger

The wedge (observed live 2026-07-09): an active profile whose refresh
chain died was never auto-switched away from. A broken active can never
produce a Fresh usage read again, and its frozen store entry is a lapsed
5h window that reads as idle headroom — so `scan_auto_switch` (demands a
Fresh active read) and `next_auto_switch_target` (demands exhaustion) both
stalled, and the daemon sat on the corpse while a viable sibling idled.

Three gate changes let a broken active drive the walk while keeping
wrap-off honest:
- `scan_auto_switch` bypasses the `decision_fresh` gate for an auth-broken
  active (the login is dead — a Fresh read will never come).
- `next_auto_switch_target` splits the exhaustion gate: `active_broken`
  OR `active_exhausted` opens the walk, but the wrap-off (halt-all) leg
  now keys on `active_exhausted` only — the flag alone never halts a
  possibly-healthy live session over spent quota it doesn't have.
- `auto_switch_if_needed` gains the same TUI-side parity guard
  (`!is_auth_broken(active) && !is_exhausted_active(...)`).

Reauth already lifts the quarantine on this branch (`overwrite_captured_
profile` clears `auth_broken` + saves, from the AUTH-3 work), so no
source change was needed there.

feat(daemon): headless scheduler + status feed, tui stand-down (#27)

* feat(daemon): headless scheduler + status.json feed, TUI stand-down (#27 a+b)

The (a)+(b) cut accepted on #27, built to the contract posted there
(now docs/daemon.md). No socket, no external mutation surface: anything
that needs eyes — a diverged live login, a manual /login, an unprovable
identity — is refused and logged; the TUI stays the only resolution
surface.

- `clauth daemon`: runs the exact same `spawn_refresher` the TUI runs
  (no `if daemon` branches in the scheduler); each 1s tick reloads
  external config changes, executes queued auto-switches / wrap-offs,
  and atomically rewrites ~/.clauth/status.json (0600, tmp+rename,
  token-free). Singleton advisory lock with standby takeover; anti-wedge
  watchdog (a stuck tick aborts for a clean supervisor restart; a failed
  watchdog spawn is loudly logged, never swallowed); size-capped
  daemon.log; ~/.clauth tightened to 0700 on boot.
- `clauth status --json`: the same serializer, single-shot from the
  on-disk caches — no daemon, no network. One code path builds both, so
  the feed and the CLI snapshot cannot drift.
- status.json: schema 1, additive-evolution rule (writers add fields
  under the same schema; readers ignore unknowns, default absents, and
  refuse only on a newer schema). Field-by-field contract in
  docs/daemon.md; the shape test pins the exact key sets.
- Dual-scheduler dedup (the condition for this landing): the TUI probes
  the singleton flock + feed freshness every tick and stands its own
  refresher down while a daemon is live — hydrating its stores from the
  disk caches the daemon keeps fresh instead of double-polling the
  usage API, double-rotating single-use refresh chains, or re-deciding
  switches — and re-arms within one tick of the daemon dying (flock
  released) or wedging (stale generated_at; the 30s window deliberately
  undercuts the 60s watchdog — the bounded overlap is documented). The
  daemon never probes: its own held flock would read as "another
  daemon". Transition logs stay off a live terminal (the TUI's stderr
  IS the ratatui screen).
- Failed switches retry on a deduped exponential backoff with a 120s
  give-up window per target, enforced at the gate too (a capped backoff
  step near the window's edge can't outlive the TTL) — one log line per
  distinct reason, never 1/tick.
- logline!: every daemon-visible stderr line gets an ISO-8601 UTC
  prefix, enabled only in daemon mode (interactive stderr stays bare).
- collect_tokens moves from tui/app.rs into the scheduler and takes
  &AppConfig — one definition shared by the TUI and the daemon. The mcp
  server's private provider/tier/windows JSON helpers consolidate into
  the new profile_json module the daemon serializer uses, so the three
  JSON surfaces genuinely share one shape.

734 tests green (daemon drains, status shape + exact key sets, probe
truth table, stand-down hydrate, backoff TTL edge, watchdog, log
rotation), clippy clean.

fix(daemon): don't defer switches behind Claude Code's logged-out shell

When Claude Code's own token refresh dies it does not delete the live

expiresAt, and keeps unrelated keys like mcpOAuth in place. That
logged-out shell still classifies LinkState::Diverged, so every guard
built on "diverged and unsaved" treated it as a login someone must
resolve: the daemon deferred every queued auto-switch ("unsaved
credentials; resolve in the TUI"), switch_profile's non-force link

running sessions sat at "Login expired" behind an empty file on a
headless box (observed 2026-07-15).

The divergence guards exist to protect a live login the operator may
hold nowhere else. A shell holds no login, so it forfeits that
protection: a new claude::live_login_is_empty / live_credentials_are_shell
pair exempts the shell from every "unsaved credentials" predicate (the
daemon deferral, the TUI twin, switch_profile's uncaptured-relogin
guard, the CLI reconcile prompt, the headless divergence default) and
from the TUI's 1Hz divergence banner. A queued switch now proceeds and
the normal install replaces the shell wholesale; a configured
default_divergence can no longer "capture" blank tokens over a
profile's stored chain.

The mid-write caution is retained: only a file that PARSES to an empty
login is a shell. An unreadable or torn live file is possibly a login
mid-write, so it keeps the full deferral, exactly like a real diverged
login (pinned by drain_pending_switch_still_defers_on_a_torn_live_file).

fix(switch): a clauth-owned live symlink is never "unsaved credentials"

Capturing a setup-token sidecar for the ACTIVE profile flips
install_source_path from credentials.json to session-token.json while the
live slot still holds the old symlink. classify_credentials_link rightly
reads Diverged — the link no longer points at what a switch installs — but
active_diverged_unsaved treated that as a login needing protection: every
unattended switch failed "unsaved credentials; resolve in the TUI" until
its retry TTL, switch-off was skipped, and the TUI prompted about
credentials that are fully saved (hit live 2026-07-21 while repairing a
mis-filled sidecar on the macOS fork).

A clauth-owned symlink's content is a profile store by construction —
re-pointing it loses nothing. New live_login_is_clauth_symlink() exempts
it in both unsaved gates (daemon + TUI); regular-file live logins (a real
CC /login) are gated exactly as before. Regression test pins the
Diverged-but-not-unsaved transition state.

fix(switch): the clauth-symlink exemption reaches all the unsaved gates

ea44696 exempted a clauth-owned live symlink from the two
active_diverged_unsaved gates (daemon + TUI), but three more spots ran the
same Diverged && !is_first_login && !live_credentials_are_shell triple and
still misfired on the stale symlink: switch_profile_cli raised a spurious
"'X' has a newer login ... [Y/n]" prompt, switch_profile_noninteractive
(the MCP switch tool) bailed "has a login clauth hasn't saved", and
poll_credentials_divergence repainted the divergence banner every second.

Collapse the triple + the symlink term into one
claude::live_diverged_and_unsaved so the exemption cannot drift back out of
sync. The daemon/TUI gates and both actions.rs switch paths route through
it; poll_credentials_divergence interleaves the first-login adoption, so it
keeps its cascade and applies the same live_login_is_clauth_symlink
exemption as its own early return. switch_profile's uncaptured-relogin
branch keeps the bare triple — a symlink repoints either way there, so the
exemption would be a no-op.

Regression test drains a queued switch over a stale clauth symlink (the
setup-token-sidecar transition state) and asserts it proceeds; a poll
sibling asserts the 1Hz banner stays clear. Both go red without the term.

fix(daemon): keep the `--status` pid in an unlocked sidecar

Windows locks are mandatory, so a `--status` reader in another process
couldn't read the pid stamped inside the daemon's held exclusive lock.
docs(daemon): note the pid moved to the `clauthd.pid` sidecar

fix(switch): the unsaved exemption is content-based, not symlink-identity

Round-2 review: the exemption keyed on `is_symlink()`, but macOS mostly
isn't a symlink. Claude Code rewrites `~/.claude/.credentials.json` as a
regular-file mirror of the Keychain after every run, clobbering our symlink.
Once a `setup-token` capture flips the active profile's install source, that
mirror classifies Diverged, `is_symlink()` reads false, and the switch
defers / the banner nags exactly as before — the same misfire, macOS again,
in the steady state rather than the pre-clobber window the 2026-07-21 repro
caught.

`live_login_is_clauth_symlink` becomes `live_login_is_stored(active)`: a
login is saved either structurally (a clauth-owned symlink, whose target is
a store by construction — kept for the unreadable/dangling case) or by
content (the live OAuth access token matches one of the profile's stored
credential files). The content half is cross-platform, so it covers the
macOS regular-file mirror and the Windows copy in one predicate and drops
the unix-only footnote. Both stores are checked (`credentials.json` and
`session-token.json`) so either install-source flip direction reads as saved.

Second site, same blindness: `switch_profile`'s `uncaptured_relogin` ran the
gate's `Diverged && !first-login && !shell` triple WITHOUT the exemption, so
after the flip the macOS mirror took the guarded link path and byte-rejected
the switch even though the defer gate now passed. It routes through
`live_diverged_and_unsaved` too, so a login already in the store forces the
relink and the switch lands. One predicate, every unsaved gate.

Tests: a cross-platform regular-file-mirror case on the helper, the daemon
drain-switch, and the 1Hz poll — all three red without the content half; the
daemon case also reds if `uncaptured_relogin` keeps the raw triple. The
symlink cases stay (now via `live_login_is_stored`), plus a dangling-symlink
assertion for the structural half.

daemon and claims, guarding it is a live clauth daemon by argv, not name.

feat(start): move a live session onto another chain member

marker stamp, link repoint and registry write, so no tick can see the

every member visited stay held for the session's life: nothing can observe
when the live child stops using a refresh token it was handed.

fix(start): keep a session's swap consistent when a step fails

Publish the new member only once the link has actually moved: a cell ahead
of the link is unretryable and turns the next tick into a cross-member
credential write. A member the session already ran on is recognized as its
own marker holder rather than a foreign one, so a swap back onto a
recovered account works at all.

fix(start): stamp the swapped store from the clock, not the old one

The mtime check Claude Code runs is an inequality, so ordering bought
nothing while an old store ahead of the clock pushed the new one past it —
and a store in the future discards every later staged rotation and re-login
on that account. Reach past the memoized value only if the filesystem
truncated onto it.

followed by holder_pid() returning None — a hard bail naming a daemon that
isn't there. Retry on the CLAIM_ATTEMPTS×CLAIM_RETRY schedule matching the
existing claim_singleton retry; a real holder keeps its lock for the process
lifetime, so only a reader clears on retry.

perf(runtime): drive credential/config reconcile off filesystem events

Replace the 100ms/1s fixed-rate polling loop in each watchdog thread with
notify-based file watching. On each event burst (debounced 200ms), run the
three reconcilers at once. A 30s fallback ticker ensures no lost event can
starve reconcile. Falls back to the original polling when notify is
unavailable (inotify limit, unsupported platform).

Adds src/watchdog.rs wrapper (try_start, watch_paths, constants) plus
crossbeam-channel for the select! multiplex. notify watches individual
files (NonRecursive) only.

The sidecar rides the reload fingerprint as its parsed status: a swap onto

Every watched file is published by rename, which unlinks the inode the

the same tick aliases onto it and would resolve back past itself.

feat(fallback): opt-in return to a preferred (home) account

Add a per-account `preferred` toggle on the Fallback card: mark one chain
member the home account, and when live work has drifted off it onto a later
member and it reads clear and fresh again, the daemon walks the active — and
every following session — back to it. Replaces the rate/greedy metric.

The return is self-limiting rather than timed: it fires only when preferred is
clear AND the active is not itself preferred, so the instant it lands the
`pref != active` guard bars any re-fire — no dwell timer, no hysteresis. Had
preferred stayed clear, the exhaustion walk could only ever have left it when
preferred was the spent member, so a clear preferred that is not the active
means work drifted off on preferred's own exhaustion and can come home.

Freshness is a HARD gate on both sides, unlike the exhaustion walk where target
freshness is only a preference: a healthy active has no forced escape to
preserve, so a stale/Cached preferred must not pull work onto a near-blocked
account, and a stuck-RateLimited active (never in `fresh`) is never moved on
numbers the scheduler declared untrustworthy. Both the global and per-session
legs carry the pass via the shared snapshot builder. Preferred also wins
wrap-off recovery — `find_recovered_member` re-arms onto it over a lower-priority
scoped-clear member.

`preferred` is exclusive across the chain (a radio, like `last_resort`) and
mutually exclusive with it — each mark clears the other. The toggle reads as a
pure on/off row, with no Config-tab counterpart. Toast and Overview wording
distinguish a homecoming from an exhaustion switch, and the `--with-fallback`
help text now names the return.

refactor(runtime): narrow the live-session rotation refusal to what the session holds

`rotation_blocked_for` refuses every rotation on macOS while a `clauth start`
session is live. Its doc comment is specific about why: that session's Claude
Code holds the pair in a Keychain item namespaced per `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`,
which clauth never writes, so a rotation leaves it spending a superseded
refresh token, and the `invalid_grant` that follows passes its own CAS guard,
blanks the pair, and signs the session out mid-task.

Every step of that mechanism needs a refresh token to attempt. A session
launched on a `session-token.json` sidecar has none — #53 put it there
precisely so sessions hold nothing rotatable — so there is nothing for it to
spend and nothing for a rotation to strand. Today such a session freezes all
four rotation legs for its profile anyway, and the profile's access token then
dies at its 8h mark for want of a rotation that was never unsafe.

So the refusal keeps its shape and loses only the sessions the mechanism cannot
reach. `live_session_holds_rotatable` reads what each live session LAUNCHED on
and refuses unless every one of them is refresh-less.

That fact did not exist anywhere, so `LiveSession` gains `launch_store`: the
credential source `acquire` resolved for the session, written from the same
value the runtime tree is built from, so the row cannot disagree with what the
session actually reads. It stores the PATH, not a verdict. The content there
can change under a running session — `claude::heal_misfilled_sidecar` exists
because a rotating pair can land in a sidecar — so a bool frozen at launch
would keep answering "refresh-less" while the file the session reads holds a
live chain. The test is made at rotation time instead.

Feed-agnostic by construction: it asks what the session HOLDS, never whether
any feature is on. A plain `claude setup-token` profile answers the same way,
and gets the same exemption for the same reason, which makes this a narrowing
of one predicate rather than a carve-out beside it. It is also the only reason
`rotation_blocked_for` can stay the single site every refusal goes through.

Every unknown reads as rotatable, matching `has_live_session`'s existing
fail-closed asymmetry: an unreadable marker dir, a marker whose name is not a
session id, a marker with no row (`acquire` deliberately tolerates a failed
registration), a row predating the field via `serde(default)`, and a
half-written credential file all refuse exactly as today. Six tests pin those
directions; a seventh, macOS-gated, pins that the narrowing is WIRED into
`rotation_blocked_for` rather than merely defined — without it, deleting the
conjunct leaves the other six green, which I verified by mutation.

Cost is one registry read plus one credential parse per live session, paid only
on macOS and only after `has_live_session` has already said yes — that is, only
on a profile that was about to be refused anyway.

feat(claude): rolling session token — plan-capable session bearers without giving back the split

The sequel to #53. The split stopped the refresh-race deaths by putting a static
`claude setup-token` mint in front of sessions, but that mint carries only
`user:inference` + `user:sessions:claude_code` and no `subscriptionType`, so the
API cannot tell which plan is behind it and plan-gated models get capped in a
clauth-managed session. The practical workaround was to stop using the split on
the accounts where it mattered most, which is backwards.

`clauth rolling-token <profile>` fixes that without giving the protection back:
the daemon re-stamps `session-token.json` from the profile's own clauth-private
usage chain — that chain's current access token, real expiry, full scopes, and
the account's `subscriptionType`, and NO refresh token. `session_token_status`
still classifies it `LongLived`, so every guard #53 added keeps working
unmodified. Sessions still hold nothing rotatable and still cannot race the
refresher; they just hold a bearer the API recognizes as the plan it actually
is. `clauth static-token <profile>` is the inverse.

Two verbs, not `on|off`, matching `disable`/`enable` — the only precedent in
this grammar for toggling per-profile state. It also answers the question of
whether this should ride the bare `clauth <profile>` form as a flag: it should
not. That form is `#[command(external_subcommand)]` and rejects a second token
with exit 2 (pinned by `an_unrecognized_multi_word_invocation_is_a_usage_error`
and `a_bare_unknown_word_exits_2`), so a flag there means hand-parsing argv
again — and it performs a mutating switch, so a flag on it would bundle two
unrelated effects on one invocation.

Telling "a mint to back up and supersede" from "a rolling bearer never to
snapshot" was an inference: a 30-day horizon plus `subscriptionType`. It is
wrong on both sides of itself. Under the horizon a real mint reads as rolling,
so it is destroyed with no backup in exactly the month a backup matters most.
Over it a fresh mint reads as not-rolling.

So the sidecar gets a marker, and it lives OUTSIDE the sidecar's wire shape —
`session-token.kind`, one word beside the file it describes. Not in the sidecar
JSON, which Claude Code and external readers consume; not in `config.toml`,
which would put a new failure mode on the `--setup-token` capture path that
profiles never using this feature also take, and which an older binary would
drop rather than ignore.

The ordering rule is the load-bearing part: the marker may only read `mint`
while the sidecar has definitely been a mint since it was written. A rolling
write marks BEFORE, a mint write marks AFTER, so a crash between the two always
lands on the same side — a claim of "rolling" over a sidecar that is still a
mint, costing at worst a skipped backup the next write repairs. The other order
would snapshot a dies-in-hours bearer as "the mint", and a restore from that
installs a dead token.

UNMARKED keeps today's heuristic rather than resolving to either answer. Every
sidecar in the field predates the marker, so resolving unmarked to `mint` would
let the first rotation after an upgrade snapshot an in-flight rolling bearer as
the degrade backup — permanently, since a backup is never replaced. There the
heuristic is not a second source of truth, it is the only one.

test(completions): parse every completion script in its own shell

The grammar walk in this file compares clap's command tree against the script
TEXT with `str::contains`. It models no shell lexical state at all, so a
quoting break is invisible to it — and worse, it DEMANDS the offending line be
present, so the assertion that should have caught the apostrophe in
`'feed[feed a profile's …]'` is the one that certified it. `offers_token`'s own
boundary predicate treats `'` as a word boundary, so the token matched cleanly
out of a string that had already terminated.

That shipped a zsh script which does not parse. `clauth completions install
zsh` writes it and sources it from the user's rc, so the blast radius was
completion for the entire `clauth` command plus a parse error on every new
shell — not just the new verb.

The only thing that can see that class is the shell itself, so each dialect's
script now goes through its own parser: `bash -n`, `zsh -n`,
`fish --no-execute`.

Three details that decide whether this is worth anything:

- A skip must not be able to pass. nextest discards a passing test's output, so
  an `eprintln!` skip is silent under exactly the runner CI uses. CI installs
  zsh and fish (neither is in the runner images; macOS ships zsh as an OS
  component, not an image addition) and sets `CLAUTH_REQUIRE_SHELL_LINT=1`,
  which turns a missing shell into a failure there while a dev box without fish
  still gets a useful run. A floor assertion catches a host with no shell at
  all. `#[ignore]` would have been worse than nothing: nothing passes
  `--run-ignored`, so it would never have run anywhere.
- zsh reports where it ran out of input, not where the quote opened — on the
  real regression it said line 65, the closing brace, for a fault on line 13. So
  the failure message scans for odd single-quote parity itself and names the
  line, with the reason a backslash cannot fix it.
- A mutation guard runs a deliberately-broken fixture through `zsh -n` and
  asserts it is REJECTED, so a refactor that swallows the exit status cannot
  turn the leg into a permanently green no-op. That is how the first one
  shipped.

Plus a portable backstop that runs with no shell installed and on the Windows
leg: odd-quote parity over the ZSH const only. Scoped deliberately — the same
scan over FISH false-positives on `-d "…that profile's runtime"`, where the
apostrophe is legitimately inside double quotes.

fix(runtime): never materialize a copy_file publish in flight

`union_children` already skips staging siblings for the watchdog mirror, and
its comment says exactly why: a shared fake-mode tree has one or several
`copy_file` publishes running at any moment, so a walk can meet a
`.tmp.<pid>.<seq>` that is about to be renamed away — walking it either fails
on the vanished source or lands an orphan nothing ever removes, since the
mirror never deletes.

Two walks on the acquire side have the same exposure and no such skip, and
there the consequence is worse because they PROPAGATE their error: the whole
`ProfileRuntime::acquire` fails, rather than a tick that would have
re-converged. On Windows it is reliable rather than theoretical, because the
publishing thread still holds the staging file open and the copy fails with
"the process cannot access the file because it is being used by another
process".

  staging sibling is a child of `~/.claude`, so it enters `pending` and gets
  materialized. Skipping it matters in real mode too — a symlink to a path
  about to be renamed away is no better than a failed copy.
- `copy_tree`'s recursion, for the same reason one level down.

Surfaced on a Windows CI leg in
`fake_mode_second_session_does_not_rebuild_the_tree`: the test writes a
sentinel into the runtime, the fake-mode watchdog's lockless `mirror_tree`
begins publishing it back into `~/.claude`, and the second acquire meets that
publish mid-flight. The same test passed in the release leg minutes earlier on
the same runner, which is what a race looks like rather than a break.

  only: a mint-SHAPED sidecar is preserved whatever the marker claims, so a
  stale marker can never be load-bearing. The reverse veto would be wrong,

(the same daemon-fights-operator failure the restore's flag-off-first
ordering exists for), and the preserved mint backup keeps the actual
year-scale credential on disk under a command that just printed
"cleared". So the clear — CLI and TUI both — takes all three pieces
together: flag first, then sidecar, then backup, serialized on the
rotation guard like the restore. "Nothing to clear" now means all three
absent, or a set flag with no files would be told nothing needs doing
while the daemon re-creates it; and the other-login guard covers the
backup slot, which the bare verb can restore into the only credential.

A deliberate asymmetry: the backup is DELETED, not quarantined.
Quarantine preserves evidence of an anomaly; an operator-confirmed
removal of their own credential is the one path where keeping the bytes
would defeat the command.

fix(rolling-token): the round-6 findings — a leash that watches, one grace, pinned copy

The long leash's exit is the operator's fix now, not the clock. The two
comments claiming a re-login re-stamps CLI-side were wrong — the browser
path writes credentials.json and nothing else, and --setup-token writes
a MINT — so every six-hour hold records a fingerprint (mtime + length)
of the profile's three credential files, and a change to any of them
releases the hold on the next scan: the gate runs right after the
re-login instead of up to six hours later. Both comments now say what is
actually true.

And the leash lands on states the daemon can act on, because the due
predicate reads a mis-fill as due NOW: the content is the defect, its
clock is irrelevant, and this leg is the only one a running daemon has
that can repair it. That takes the round-5 arm from defensive structure
to the actual repair path — a mis-filled sidecar beside a healthy
preserved mint heals without anyone switching, and the no-backup case
answers SidecarMisfilled onto the watched leash, which the prescribed
re-mint then releases.

AUTH_GATE_GRACE_MS is BACKUP_EXPIRY_GRACE_MS now — one number, one home.
Sixty seconds beside the same commit's five-minute argument meant a mint
with three minutes of life exited 1 as EXPIRED from static-token while a
switch installed the identical bytes. Every consumer moves toward Claude
Code's real refresh threshold, and all five were walked before the
number: vanilla_install_gate's comfortable-chain test, sidecar_live,
rolling_fresh on the switch path, gate_under_guard, and
roll_from_stored_chain's staleness gate.

A failed sidecar repair distinguishes contention from fault: the repair
bodies run under with_state_lock, whose bounded flock wait times out
while a sibling process is merely busy (on macOS, across a 20-second
Keychain shell-out) — rendering that as SidecarWriteFailed's "check
permissions" sent the operator hunting a fault that does not exist. A
StateLockTimeout anywhere in the chain now reads as StateLockBusy, the
same contention-vs-fault split as rounds 1 and 3, one lock further down.

The four measured survivors are dead: the scope-widening disclosure, the
three DaemonHealth claims, and the stranded-rollback warning are each a
single-caller fn — content unit-pinned, and a deleted print is now a
dead-code error under -D warnings rather than a silent posture change.
The sub-hour re-stamp band has its strictly-inside fixture, and the
stalled-rolling fix line is pinned to snap.title through the draft-open
shape that blanks snap.name. lockorder's RollingPacing list names all
four acquisition sites again.

fix(rolling-token): what the verification fleet caught in the round-6 commits

Six confirmed findings in my own reconcile and round-6 commits, the
worst self-inflicted this series has produced:

- THE CRITICAL: `--clear` (and the bare restore) persisted the flag flip
  by writing the pre-acquire config snapshot back through save_profile —
  which persists the WHOLE profile. On the clear that snapshot predates
  an UNBOUNDED confirm prompt, so a rotation landing while the operator
  thinks rewinds credentials.json to a spent refresh token: the exact
  chain-death class this whole series exists to prevent, minted by the
  command's own hand. Both paths now re-read the profile from disk under
  the rotation guard and write only the flag; the relink decision
  re-reads `active` the same way (a switch during the prompt otherwise
  dangles the live symlink in one direction and steals it in the other).

- The TUI clear claimed the CLI's full-exit contract while missing the
  two pieces that make it one: it now takes the rotation guard
  NON-BLOCKING (try_acquire — a UI thread never parks on a timeout-less
  flock, and a held guard fails loudly into a toast with nothing moved),
  and the clear row is offered whenever ANY long-lived piece exists
  (sidecar, backup, or a set flag — the flag-only state previously had
  no TUI surface left to remove it). Its persist reads the disk under
  the guard like the CLI's, and its hint now DISCLOSES the full scope —
  re-stamping stops, the preserved mint goes too — because a two-press
  arm is not a disclosure.

- A mis-filled sidecar is quarantined by the clear, not plain-deleted:
  it is the anomaly the split exists to detect, the operator did not
  name it (the prompt says "the long-lived token"; a rotating pair is
  precisely not that), and every other disposal path moves it aside.

- The one arm that INSTALLS a mint read its clock with zero grace while
  every other verdict on the same bytes used CC's five-minute threshold
  — so `clauth static-token` called a file EXPIRED that the very next
  switch served happily, the exact split the review's hold #2 named.
  `vanilla_install_gate`'s static arm is the sixth consumer now, pinned
  in both directions.

- The backwards-clock clamp stretched SHORT holds onto the six-hour
  bound with no credential watch — the one combination with no exit but
  the clock. The hold knows its kind now (`watched` rides the long
  leash), so each kind clamps to its own bound, and the old "the stamp
  does not say which leash minted it" rationale is retired with it.

- The watch comments overclaimed "the operator's fix": clauth's own
  successful rotation also moves the fingerprint, and that is a feature
  (a chain that just rotated is worth re-judging), so the comments now
  say so instead of promising an operator-only trigger.

Plus the sweep: the three clear copy lines are single-caller fns with
content pins (same argument as the arm report — no stdout capture
exists), the nothing-to-clear no-op is pinned by the rotation lock file
the full path cannot avoid creating, --help stopped implying the mint
survives a --clear, the stale 60s/seconds-tight grace comments are
gone, `restamp_due`'s own test states the mis-fill arm instead of
contradicting it, and the session_tokens cache drops the SidecarKind
half that upstream's 5dde024 orphaned.

fix(rolling-token): the round-7 findings — a postscript for --yes, one refusal condition, a kind that is passed

The one ask: a scripted `--clear` destroyed the preserved mint — a
year-scale credential — with nothing saying so, because both pre-prompt
notes print inside the interactive branch that `--yes` skips. The
removal now has an unconditional postscript on both surfaces, mirroring
the disarm one: `clear_backup_postscript` on the CLI, gated only on a
backup actually having been removed, and a ` · the preserved mint is
gone` toast suffix on the TUI.

The measured items, all taken:

- The three clear copy fns (and the new postscript) carry CONTENT pins
  now — single-caller keeps a deleted print a dead-code error, but only
  a pin keeps the words, and both pre-prompt lines are TTY-only so no
  behavioral test ever executes them.

- The TUI clear persists the flag BEFORE flipping the renderer's
  in-memory copy. Flipped first, a failed save leaves `app.config()`
  lying against the disk — `reload_fingerprint` never corrects it
  (config mtime did not move) and a later unrelated save makes the lie
  durable: a live rolling sidecar nothing re-stamps. Pinned by failing
  the persist stage alone (a directory where config.toml should be).

- The CLI and the TUI refuse on the SAME condition now: only a stored
  PIECE (sidecar or preserved mint) is a credential to strip, so a
  flag-only account with no other login disarms on both surfaces
  instead of getting a visible row with a silent return. The hint's
  gate arm reads the identical condition — a gate line over a row that
  acts would be the one lie a hint can tell.

- The other-login refusal is re-checked UNDER the rotation guard from
  the same disk read the flag write uses: the prompt is an unbounded
  wait a log-out can land inside, and this is the one decision that can
  strip a profile's last credential. Driven through the guard itself in
  its test — the clear parks on `acquire` while the login is removed.

- `cmd_static_token_clear` reads the backup slot through
  `claude::has_static_backup` instead of a second inline spelling that
  disagreed on the `profile_dir` error arm.

- `retry_hold` takes the hold's KIND (`HoldKind`) instead of inferring
  it back from `retry_ms == ROLLING_BROKEN_RETRY_MS` — every call site
  already knows which it is minting, and a numeric coincidence breaks
  silently the first time a non-re-login verdict wants a long leash.
  Duration and watch both derive from the kind, so they cannot disagree.

- The widened row gate has fixtures for each arm alone: a set flag with
  nothing stamped, and a preserved mint alone, each keep the row; flag
  down with nothing stored drops it.

fix(rolling-token): what the verification fleet caught in the round-7 commits

Eighteen upheld findings from the pre-push adversarial pass over the
round-7 diff and the rebase weave; the ones that matter:

- Two stamp paths decided "this profile is rolling" from a PRE-guard
  read and never re-checked the flag once they held the guard — so a
  writer parked on the guard (the start-time arming leg, or a gate
  routed from the daemon's in-memory config) would re-stamp a fresh
  rolling bearer over a COMPLETED clear: flag off, nothing ever
  re-stamps it, backup already destroyed — a dies-in-hours credential
  with no exit, re-created after the operator was told it was gone.
  Both `arm_rolling_from_disk` and `rolling_install_gate` now re-read
  the flag from disk under the guard; the gate's Block leg drops the
  guard and falls to the vanilla install, the NoWait leg reports Ready
  (its still-due re-read then drops the pacing hold). Pinned by the
  Barrier seam on the arm leg and a stale-in-memory-config fixture on
  both gate legs.

- The TUI's other-login refusal read a snapshot `reload_fingerprint`
  can never invalidate (it does not stat credentials.json), so an
  out-of-band log-out left the gate waving the clear through into
  stripping the account's last credential — indefinitely, not for one
  tick. The refusal is re-checked from disk under the guard, exactly
  like the CLI's; `rolling_armed` rides the same under-guard read.
  `active` deliberately stays the in-memory read: the TUI is itself
  the thing that switches in this process, and upstream's tests pin
  that semantics.

- Both surfaces removed the sidecar first and relinked LAST, so a
  backup-removal failure in between left an active profile's live
  slot a dangling symlink under a toast reading "clear failed" — a
  broken login reported as nothing-happened. The relink now lands
  before the backup removal, and a failed removal owns the partial
  state in its own words on both surfaces. Driven by a directory
  blocking the backup slot.

- The third reader of the clear gate — `detail_row`'s dim — was still
  on the old unconditional condition, so a flag-only account rendered
  faint/inert while its press acted, and the first press armed
  invisibly. `Snap::clear_gated` is the one spelling both render
  readers share now, and the widened state renders the acting button.

- The widened clear told a credential-less account it "runs on its api
  key" — a claim about a credential that does not exist, on the hint,
  the toast, and the CLI line alike. The flag-only-no-login state has
  its own copy on all three now, naming the sign-out when active.

- Test honesty: the backup toast suffix has its absent-case pin, the
  postscript GATING is pinned as a value (`clear_postscripts`), the
  guard-race test retries until the under-guard leg provably fired
  (its "anymore" discriminator) with no panic in the detach window,
  and the union-duplicated doc block is deduped.

Also: the Quickstart refusal sentence and `has_stored_oauth_login`'s
doc now state the piece-gated refusal instead of the retired
unconditional one.

feat(codex): the standby refresh — codex's own discipline, the belt, the kick

The codex plan's phase 4 core. codex_auth is the credential engine:

- The auth model keeps the WHOLE value and rewrites read-modify-write, so
  every key a newer codex writes survives a clauth rotation; the access
  token's exp is an unverified JWT read (it feeds a schedule, never an
  authorization). The refresh wire is the spec's verified contract — three
  fields, JSON — against the shared agent, with failures classified the
  way codex's own manager classifies them and an unrecognized 4xx read as
  DEAD rather than replayed against a single-use chain.
- The standby leg (a self-contained daemon tick pass over the codex
  roster; the claude scheduler is untouched — decision 4) rotates a chain
  inside a ten-minute lead, twice codex's own five-minute window. The
  no-replay rule is an attempt memo: a failed refresh persists nothing
  and the SAME token never feeds the routine leg again — only the health
  kick may retry it, one forced attempt per kick, two consecutive kicks
  at most (the #51 breaker), reset by a successful poll. The stand-down
  is scoped exactly as accepted on #51: only a profile with a LIVE codex
  session has a codex to lose the pre-expiry race to; a parked profile
  rotates right through that window, because waiting there is how parked
  chains died at the wham 401 (the fork's EXP-1 finding). Only the
  post-guard re-read feeds the wire, and a token that changed while we
  decided means somebody healthier already rotated.
- The belt, as accepted on #51: every well-formed store read records a
  last-known-good copy (atomic, 0600, never linked — it cannot become a
  carrier), and a store that reads bad twice IN A ROW ACROSS a guard
  acquisition — a live in-place write cannot span one — is restored from
  it. The window it cannot close (a crash between codex's truncate and
  its write of a newly rotated pair) fails exactly the way doing nothing
  fails, so the belt is strictly better than nothing and never worse.
- The one failure worth shouting is shouted: a rotation that SUCCEEDED on
  the wire but could not land in the store names the consequence (the
  chain will read as reused) and the fix, instead of a generic IO error.

Capture now parses through the same CodexAuth model — one parser, and the
identity guard reads account_id off it.

single-use chain or a durable DB surviving something clauth did not
model.

moves the LINK and leaves the corrupt bytes in the profile store
untouched; codex's fresh DB then lives only in the session home and dies
at teardown, and the next session relinks to the same corruption and
recovers again, forever. Teardown now carries back any durable entry
that has become a regular FILE where the build placed a link — which is
exactly codex's recovery signature.

Decision 8 permits concurrent codex sessions BECAUSE they share one
physical auth.json; under Fake they share nothing, since the flavors
collapse to different bare stems and each holds its own copy converged
from the same store. Two live flavors are then two carriers of one
single-use rotating chain, with no reload-and-skip between them (codex's
own answer needs one inode), so the first refresh on either side strands

feat(codex): the usage leg — wham/usage, the chain, and the kick's producer

Phase 5. codex accounts now poll their own usage, feed the same named
window model claude fills, and rotate on their own chain.

The body is DURATION-keyed, never name-keyed — it says "a window of N
seconds is P percent spent", never "this is the weekly one" — so
`usage/codex.rs` is where a duration becomes one of clauth's two named
slots. Over a day is weekly, under it is the 5h slot, position breaks a
tie (primary is the short one), and two windows naming one slot do not
overwrite each other: the second takes the free slot, because dropping
it would silently lose the tighter of two real limits. `reset_at` is the
server's absolute answer and wins over `reset_after_seconds`, so clock
skew cannot move a reset the server stated.

`limit_reached` is a HARD verdict and outranks the percentages it came
with: an account blocked at 96% would otherwise sit under every
threshold and keep being chosen. The block lands on the fuller window
and is never fabricated onto one the body did not send.

`plan_type` is held verbatim in a new `PlanInfo.codex_plan` rather than
folded into `PlanTier`, whose every label spells "Claude <tier>" — which
would render a ChatGPT Pro account as Claude Pro. Banked reset credits
ride the same response, so reading them costs no extra request; clauth
reads the count and never spends one.

Readings land in the SHARED UsageStore, keyed by name. Safe by
construction rather than convention: names are globally unique across
both state files (decision 2), and the claude walk only ever indexes the
map by its own members, so a codex entry is inert there while every
read-only surface gets codex for free.

The chain is built from `codex-profiles.toml` alone (decision 4) with
`check_scoped` disarmed — per-model weekly windows are an anthropic

the codex active slot and lands at the NEXT codex session; there is no
executor, because codex binds auth.json at start.

Folded fix 1 is answered where it bites rather than by changing a shared
predicate: a member with no usage entry reads as un-exhausted, which is

feat(selection): choose the account at session start by the models it will run

The chain decides where a session MOVES; nothing decided where it STARTS. So a
`weekly_scoped` window has to be a blanket exclusion — `scoped_weekly_blocked_info`
says it outright: the walk cannot know which model the next session runs.
`check_scoped = false` is the only escape and it is all-or-nothing, so a session of
the capped model can then be routed onto a member that cannot serve it.

A session that has not started yet is the one case where the model IS knowable.
`clauth start --auto` weighs the chain against the model families this session may
run and starts on the best member that can serve all of them, so an account capped
only on a per-model week it will never touch stops being excluded from work it
could do.

Deliberately start-time only. Cache entries do not cross accounts, so a switch
mid-session re-sends the whole context as fresh input; the chain pays that to
rescue a spent account, but it is a bad way to optimise. Nothing here moves a
running session, and `--with-fallback` is untouched — the two compose.

Selection is on the UNION of families, not the headline model. A `Task` subagent
runs inside the parent process and spends the parent's account on whatever model it
runs, so choosing for the main thread alone would strand the session the moment a
subagent used a capped family. The union comes from the effective settings model,
`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, and any `--model` passed through. With none resolved
the demand is empty and today's blanket `check_scoped` behaviour stands.

Picking badly causes the exact cost this avoids — a member with minutes left
strands one turn in and the chain swaps it — so feasibility is RUNWAY (headroom
over burn, reusing `compute_burn_rates_from_history`), not utilization. Absent burn
reads as unbounded, never zero, matching `is_exhausted_projected`'s stance that a
member is never uncovered for lack of data. A window resetting inside the grace is
feasible however thin. Nothing feasible still launches, flagged, rather than
refusing.

Ranking puts live sessions ahead of runway: launching several sessions at once
would otherwise send them all to the same member, and usage polling cannot see the
launches until its next refresh. A member with no usage cache at all ranks below
one clauth has numbers for — it reports unbounded runway for want of data, not
because it is empty, which an api-key chain member would otherwise exploit to win
every selection.

`worst_scoped_window` gains a `_for` variant taking the families; the blanket
spelling delegates to it, so the narrowed judgment cannot drift from the chain's —
liveness in particular, without which an already-reset window would gate off a
stale cache.

Also: `delegate` can pick its own account when `profiles` is omitted (opt-in,
`delegate_auto_select`) — a separate process, so the one subagent that can hold
one; and `clauth start --explain` prints the decision without spending a window.

User-visible, per CONTRIBUTING:
- new `start` flags `--auto` and `--explain`, in all three completion scripts.
  `--auto` deliberately does NOT complete a profile after it: it takes the
  profile's place, so what follows belongs to `claude`.
- `--auto` needs the `--` separator when claude's first arg starts with a hyphen.
  With no name in the profile slot clap cannot tell a passthrough `-p` from a
  misspelled clauth flag; giving the positional `allow_hyphen_values` instead would
  turn `clauth start --isolatd acme` into a confusing profile-not-found.
- new `profiles.toml` keys `selection_min_runway_mins` (20),
  `selection_reset_grace_mins` (10), `delegate_auto_select` (false).
- no existing default changes; `clauth start <profile>` and the chain walk behave
  exactly as before.

Docs updated in the same change: Quickstart (flags + rules), Configuration (the
key table), Auto-Switch (the limitation passage, the `scoped gate` bullet, and a
new section), Claude-Code-Plugin (delegate targets), FAQ, README.

feat(profile): choose the home account by weekday (#77)

* feat(profile): choose the home account by weekday

`preferred` is one static flag, so an operator who wants one account home on
weekdays and another at the weekend has to run an external job that rewrites
two config.toml files twice a day.

Add a per-profile `preferred_days` list. A named day is claimed against the
whole profile list: on a day some list names, only the accounts naming it are
home, and a bare `preferred = true` elsewhere stands down for that day and
takes charge again on the days no list claims. The usual split is then one
line in one profile, and any weekday can go to any account.

Resolving this across the list rather than per profile is the point. Per
profile, the flag would keep claiming all seven days, so which account won a
Saturday would come down to chain order.

Entries parse as chrono weekdays, full or three-letter, in any case; one that
does not parse is dropped rather than failing the profile, and the canonical
rewrite then drops it from disk. `duplicate_profile` leaves the list behind
for the same reason it leaves `preferred`.

The day is read in `chain_member` and `scan_recovery`, where a ChainMember is
built, rather than at load: the hot-reload fingerprint is built from
config.toml mtimes and midnight moves no file, so a load-time fold would sit
stale until the next config write. The overview's `⌂` reads the same resolved
value, since it marks a switch that lands on home.

account leaves the chain, is disabled, its login breaks — and a hand-edited
`config.toml` never passes the editor at all. Neither reached the operator.

The notice names what became of the day, not just that a line is inert: a
carried day still has somebody home and reads as a stray line, while an
uncarried one has quietly fallen back to the flag.

Both gates now hold the SET of notices rather than one string. Two notices are
two keys: a passed-over lister arriving while a collision is still up has to
raise its own toast and leave the collision's alone, which one string would
either repaint or swallow.

The collision's daemon logline was asserted only through the gate's
transitions, which read identically if the `logline!` were dropped. It goes
through `LogLines::capture_here` now, so the emission is pinned too.

* fix(tui): name the chain, not the toggle, when a saved list claims nothing

The warning's tail promised that `preferred` still decides those days. On an
account the walk skips, the toggle is as chain-inert as the list, so nobody
decides them — the chain resolves the day among the accounts it can reach.

The comment above it cited the chain picker as the precedent for showing a
dead account rather than hiding it. `chain_candidates` filters disabled
accounts, so the picker does not list them; the reason that does hold is that
the state is reachable without this row at all.

User-visible: the second line of the warning toast on a saved list that
claims nothing.

* fix: ask the eligibility once at the entry, not once per branch

`is_home_on`'s unclaimed branch read the bare flag, so an account the walk
never visits — disabled, auth-broken, or off the chain — marked the `⌂` and
the return-to-preferred copy on every day no list claimed. The walk could
never land there, so the reading was display-only, but it named a homecoming
that cannot happen.

The claim half already had this check. Adding a second copy to the flag half
would answer the report and leave the shape that produced it: the gap WAS a
branch that did not repeat the check, and a third branch would repeat the gap.
So the eligibility moves to the entry and both branches inherit it. It is
redundant on the claimed branch, where `day_listers` has already applied it;
that redundancy is what makes the omission impossible.

`serves_the_chain` is that judgment in bool form, defined in terms of
`day_claim_blocker` — the editor needs the same question answered with its
reason — so the two cannot drift.

One behavioural change beyond the display: the soonest-weekly-reset walk is
gated on no chain member being preferred (#87), and a disabled member holding
the flag used to satisfy that gate. It no longer does, so the walk runs in a
case where it was suppressed by an account the return pass could not reach.
